q: How do we count stationery, printing paper and office supplies in Scope 3?
title: Stationery and office supplies in Scope 3
short: They are purchased goods in Category 1. Copier paper is easy to count by weight, since invoices show reams and GSM; for pens, files and toner use spend. It is a small line for factories but can matter for offices, where paper is one of the few material purchases.
audience: Admin teams in offices and factories

sections.h: Count what you can by weight
ul: Copier paper: a ream of 500 A4 sheets at 75 GSM weighs about 2.3 kg. Reams x weight x a paper factor gives an activity-based figure.
Recycled paper usually carries a lower factor than virgin; check the supplier's claim.
Envelopes and printed forms by weight where listed.
Pens, files, folders, toner and cartridges: spend excluding GST x a factor for the product group.
Printing done by an outside press: purchased service, by weight of print or spend.

p: Double-sided default printing and digital approvals reduce reams bought. Track reams per employee per year as a simple indicator.

example.title: Worked example: copier paper weight (one year)
lines: One ream: 500 x 0.0624 m2 x 75 g = 2,340 g, about 2.3 kg
Multiply by your paper factor per kg for Category 1
example.note: An A4 sheet is 0.21 m x 0.297 m = 0.0624 m2.

senseible: Senseible reads purchase and service invoices; it uses quantities where the invoice shows them and otherwise gives a spend-based estimate, labelled as spend-based with wider uncertainty.

sources.label: GHG Protocol Scope 3 Standard, Category 1 purchased goods and services
